senses.definition: A layer of material under the ground that holds water and lets enough move through to supply a well or spring.
senses.example: The well reached an aquifer with water between grains of sand.

senses.definition: A tiny living thing made of one cell. Some help other living things, while others can cause illness.
senses.example: One kind of bacterium makes food using chemicals near a deep-sea vent.

senses.definition: Long strips in some whales’ mouths that work like a strainer to catch tiny food.
senses.example: The blue whale used its baleen to hold krill while water flowed back out.

senses.definition: Light made by a living thing using a process inside its body.
senses.example: A deep-sea fish can use bioluminescence to shine in the dark.

senses.definition: A thick layer of fat under the skin that helps keep some ocean mammals warm.
senses.example: A seal has blubber between its skin and muscles.

senses.definition: A little salty, as water can be where a river mixes with the sea.
senses.example: The marsh creek held brackish water when the tide came in.

senses.definition: An underground passage or home made or used by an animal.
senses.example: The meerkat ran into its burrow when another meerkat called.

senses.definition: The breaking away of ice from the edge of a glacier to form floating pieces.
senses.example: Calving formed several new icebergs at the front of the glacier.

senses.definition: Color, shape, or pattern that makes a living thing hard to see in a place.
senses.example: The octopus used its skin color as camouflage against the rocks.

senses.definition: A hard covering over all or part of an animal’s back.
senses.example: The loggerhead’s top shell, called a carapace, is reddish brown.

senses.definition: Making food using energy from chemicals instead of energy from sunlight.
senses.example: Some bacteria at ocean vents use chemosynthesis.

senses.definition: The temperature to which air must cool before water vapor begins to turn into drops, if the amount of water in the air stays the same.
senses.example: The grass cooled to the dew point and tiny drops formed.

senses.definition: A fin that rises from the back of a swimming animal.
senses.example: The orca’s dorsal fin showed above the water.

senses.definition: A flat limb that helps an animal swim or steer.
senses.example: The sea lion pulled itself forward with its front flippers.

senses.definition: One of the broad sections of a whale’s two-part tail.
senses.example: White marks showed on the humpback whale’s flukes.

senses.definition: A picture or idea showing who eats whom among many living things in one place.
senses.example: Kelp, sea urchins, and sea otters are connected in a food web.

senses.definition: Water found below the surface in gaps in soil and rock.
senses.example: Some of the rain soaked down and became groundwater.

senses.definition: An animal that eats mainly or only plants.
senses.example: Triceratops had a beak and teeth to feed as a herbivore.

senses.definition: A place on the sea floor where hot water from below comes out through an opening.
senses.example: A hydrothermal vent released fluid carrying bits of minerals.

senses.definition: Rock made when melted material cools and becomes solid.
senses.example: Obsidian is an igneous rock that can have a glassy surface.

senses.definition: A narrow band of fast-moving air high in the sky.
senses.example: The plane flew with the jet stream and arrived sooner.

senses.definition: A kind of large brown seaweed.
senses.example: Fish hid under the long kelp blades.

senses.definition: Small swimming animals with bodies shaped a little like tiny shrimp.
senses.example: A whale took in a mouthful of water full of krill.

senses.definition: A kind of animal whose mothers feed their young milk. Mammals have hair at least at some stage in life.
senses.example: Dolphins and bears are both mammals.

senses.definition: Rock changed from an older rock by heat, pressure, or other changes inside Earth, without melting completely.
senses.example: Marble is a metamorphic rock that can form from limestone.

senses.definition: A ridge or pile of loose material carried and left by a glacier.
senses.example: The rocky moraine showed where the glacier once reached.

senses.definition: The upper part of an ocean or lake where enough sunlight can reach for many living things to use it to make food.
senses.example: Plants in the photic zone can catch sunlight under water.

senses.definition: Mostly tiny drifting living things that can make food using sunlight.
senses.example: The phytoplankton used light near the sea surface.

senses.definition: Living things that are carried by water currents instead of mostly swimming on their own.
senses.example: A manta ray strained plankton from the seawater.

senses.definition: An animal that catches and eats other animals.
senses.example: The cheetah is a predator that can run fast for a short time.

senses.definition: One of the stiff, pointed hairs of an animal such as a porcupine.
senses.example: The loose quill had a very sharp tip.

senses.definition: One of a group of dinosaurs with long necks and tails that walked on four legs and ate plants.
senses.example: Brachiosaurus was a sauropod with especially long front legs.

senses.definition: A flowering plant that grows under the sea with roots and long leaves.
senses.example: The green turtle bit off a piece of seagrass in shallow water.

senses.definition: Rock made from settled grains or from other material that collects in a layer and hardens.
senses.example: Grains of sand held together can form a sedimentary rock called sandstone.

senses.definition: A mineral formation that grows downward from the roof of a cave as water leaves material behind.
senses.example: A drop hung for a moment at the tip of a stalactite.

senses.definition: A mineral formation that grows upward from a cave floor as water drops leave material behind.
senses.example: The rounded stalagmite grew where drops hit the same spot.

senses.definition: A preserved sign of what a living thing did long ago, such as a track or burrow.
senses.example: The track in the rock is a trace fossil of a dinosaur walking.

senses.definition: A long tooth that sticks out past an animal’s mouth.
senses.example: A narwhal’s tusk is a long tooth that sticks out from its upper jaw.

senses.definition: A boundary where masses of air with different temperatures meet.
senses.example: Clouds formed where warm air rose at a weather front.

senses.definition: How hard the air pushes on something. It usually gets lower as you go higher above sea level.
senses.example: A barometer shows whether the air pressure is rising or falling.
